truths.truth: A delayed repeat close never consumes the next dispatch of the same worker key: the replay renders two brackets carrying their own figures and roles.tokens sums those two, not all three terminals.
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/trace.mjs:812-814 - `delayedRepeat` requires both clocks parsed, terminal ts strictly earlier than the head pending dispatch, and `pairedRows.has(worker)`; `matched` is null on that arm so no pending dispatch is consumed. Named test `render: a delayed repeat close never steals the NEXT dispatch of its key` (cadence-core/bin/trace.test.mjs:1689) asserts brackets.length 2, ts/end/tokens per row, ms 300000 on both (the pre-fix tell was -240000), unpaired empty and roles.tokens = a.tokens + b.tokens. Ran green together with the three shipped dedup tests and the committed-fixture test, bodies unmodified: 8/8 pass.

truths.truth: With two open dispatches of one role, a SubagentStop payload closes the dispatch whose agent_id matches rather than the newest one.
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/subagent-trace.mjs:210 `if (mine.length !== 1) return null;` - the only use of the payload id is the NEGATIVE filter `alreadyClosed` at :164/:199, which asks whether some bracket already carries the id. No code path selects among two open dispatches by id. The shipped test is `stop: TWO open dispatches of the role produce NOTHING` (cadence-core/bin/subagent-trace.test.mjs:184). Probe: closeForStop({agent_type:'cadence:cad-executor-xhigh', agent_id:'AID-1'}, <render with two open cad-executor rows>, {transcript: <end_turn>}) returned null.

truths.truth: A SubagentStop payload whose transcript shows the worker has not reached a terminal entry writes no return event at all, while an absent or unreadable transcript still writes the close it wrote before.
truths.evidence: GATE 0 at cadence-core/bin/lib/subagent-trace.mjs:187 refuses on NOT_TERMINAL only; `terminalOf` (cadence-core/bin/lib/subagent-transcript.mjs) answers not-terminal for stop_reason null and tool_use and unknown for every unreadable shape; the disk half injects the bytes (cadence-core/bin/subagent-trace.mjs readTranscript, 8 MiB ceiling). Disk-half probe on a scratch planning root: a payload pointing at a tool_use-terminated transcript left trace.jsonl at 1 line before and after; the same payload with no transcript_path appended the ordinary figureless return. 19/19 tests in subagent-trace.test.mjs and 15/15 in subagent-transcript.test.mjs pass.

truths.truth: The ordinary two-writer case is unchanged: one dispatch, a figureless hook close, then the hand-written close with figures renders one bracket with dispatches: 1.
truths.evidence: Shipped tests `render: a dispatch closed by BOTH writers is exactly one bracket`, `render: the two closes render identically in EITHER arrival order`, `render: two genuine dispatches on ONE worker key are still two brackets` and `fixture: the committed verbatim trace renders exactly as it did before this phase` all pass with bodies unmodified (git diff 2a385615..HEAD shows no hunk inside them). truths.truth: /cad-report and /cad-suggest each print a figure sourced from a bracket's duration_ms, labelled apart from the bracket's ms, and say unrecorded rather than 0 when the close carried none.

truths.truth: The worker's host id reaches the bracket row whenever either writer carried it, which is what the hook's already-closed equality test reads.

gaps.name: Stop close picks the dispatch its agent id names
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the shipped rule never picks a dispatch by agent id. With two open dispatches of one role it closes NOTHING, whatever id the payload carries. The payload's id is used only as a negative filter (has some bracket already got this id?), so the positive half of AC2, of ROADMAP success criterion 2 and of TRC-06 ('lands on the worker that actually stopped') is not delivered; only the 'never the newest open dispatch' half is.
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/subagent-trace.mjs:210 `if (mine.length !== 1) return null;` is the whole adoption rule; :164 `alreadyClosed` and :199 are the only readers of the payload id. cadence-core/bin/subagent-trace.test.mjs:184 pins the shipped behaviour by name: 'stop: TWO open dispatches of the role produce NOTHING', asserting null both with and without a terminal transcript. Probe: closeForStop with agent_id 'AID-1' against a render holding two open cad-executor rows returned null. The design change is recorded in SUMMARY Deviations (426163a0) and in the CONTEXT annotation to D-07, but no artifact re-states AC2, ROADMAP criterion 2 or TRC-06 to match what shipped.
gaps.missing: A ruling on which one moves. Either (a) accept 'unambiguous or nothing' and re-word UAT item 2, ROADMAP Phase 1 success criterion 2 and REQUIREMENTS TRC-06 to say the hook refuses on ambiguity rather than picking by id - the honest statement of the shipped rule, since the dispatch half can never carry an id - or (b) fund the positive join, which needs an id on the dispatch half or another record that pairs an agent id to a dispatch, and which the plan-1 gate already refuted twice for the parallel path.

gaps.name: The worker's host id survives whichever writer closes first
gaps.reason: unwired on the ordinary arrival order - the repeat-close fold in renderTrace does not fold agent_id, so an id supplied on the hand-written close is dropped whenever the hook's figureless close opened the bracket first. That ordering is the ordinary one (the host fires SubagentStop when the worker stops, before the orchestrator processes the return and writes its close) and is the ordering AC4 itself calls ordinary. The code comment claims the opposite of what the code does.
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/trace.mjs:866-871 says agent_id is 'OMITTED when neither writer carried it, the same rule `turns` and `duration_ms` follow'; the fold at :902-910 handles tokens, turns, duration_ms and both CACHE_KEYS and never agent_id. Probe on a scratch planning root - dispatch, figureless return, then `planning.mjs trace close --agent-id WORKER-Z --tokens 900 --turns 4 --duration-ms 60000` - rendered {tokens:900,turns:4,duration_ms:60000} with no agent_id key at all. Consequence: the record's worker identity is present only on brackets the hand-written close opened, and cadence-core/bin/lib/subagent-trace.mjs:164's equality test reads a key that is absent on the common path. The TraceRender typedef at :340 also omits agent_id from the brackets shape.
gaps.missing: Fold the id in the repeat-close arm the way turns and duration_ms are folded (`if (!('agent_id' in b) && e.agent_id) b.agent_id = e.agent_id;` beside trace.mjs:906), add agent_id to the TraceRender brackets typedef at :340, and add a render test for the hook-close-first ordering asserting the bracket carries the id the hand-written close supplied.

human_checks.name: Run a real parallel execute in this repository with the orchestrator passing `trace close --agent-id`, then read `.planning/trace.jsonl` for two brackets carrying two distinct agent ids - and note whether the host's subagent return actually surfaces an id to copy.
human_checks.expected: Two `return` events, each carrying its own `agent_id`, rendering as two brackets with distinct ids; and a late SubagentStop for either worker appends nothing. Today `grep -c agent_id .planning/trace.jsonl` is 0 over 2283 events.
human_checks.why_human: Out of reach for this pass and not merely unexercised. It needs the live host to dispatch two real subagents and to render a worker id in its return - cadence-core/references/seam-spawn-agent.md's STANDING EXPOSURE bullet lists only three figures on a return (tokens, tool uses, duration) and the SUMMARY's own open item records that the host labels the subagent id internal and instructs against surfacing it, which is why no dispatch in this phase passed one. Whether `--agent-id <the id on the subagent return>` (workflows/execute.md:230) is a flag anything can fill is decided by the host at run time, and the check also mutates this repository's real record and spends real dispatches, so I neither ran it nor simulated it. The seam itself is already proven on a scratch root; what is unproven is that the host will hand the id over.
